subject: brown-headed cowbird
title: This Bird Runs a Protection Racket. Reject Its Egg and It Wrecks Your Nest

scenes.text: This bird runs a protection racket, and other birds pay up.
The brown-headed cowbird never builds a nest. It lays its eggs in the nests of more than 100 other species and leaves.
Scientists in Illinois watched 182 warbler nests for four years. In some, they removed the cowbird egg. Then they waited.
56 percent of the nests that lost a cowbird egg were ransacked, eggs smashed or thrown out. Of the nests that kept it, only 6 percent.
Block the cowbirds from reaching the nests, and the wrecking dropped to zero. The cowbirds were coming back to check.
It works. Warblers that threw the egg out raised 60 percent fewer chicks than the ones who played along. Pay the bird, keep your nest.

description:
Brown-headed cowbirds lay their eggs in the nests of more than 100 other bird species. A study in the Cache River watershed of southern Illinois monitored 182 predator-proofed prothonotary warbler nests over four breeding seasons and removed cowbird eggs from some of them.
When cowbirds could reach the nests, 56 percent of nests that had lost a cowbird egg were ransacked, against 6 percent of nests that accepted it, and none when cowbirds were kept out. Warblers that ejected the egg ended up raising about 60 percent fewer of their own young, which is why most hosts tolerate the intruder. The work by Jeffrey Hoover and Scott Robinson was published in PNAS in 2007.
Would you pay the cowbird or risk it? Comment below.
first_comment: Cowbirds also wreck nests that have no cowbird egg at all, so the host builds a new one on a schedule the cowbird can use. Scientists call it farming. Which animal crime should we cover next?
